name: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Sukkarī
summary: Grammarian and 'transmitter of the Basrans' in Baghdad, pupil of Abū Ḥātim, al-Riyāshī and Ibn Ḥabīb, who edited the dīwāns of the great poets, the Hudhalīs and the brigand poets.
bio: Al-Sukkarī took from Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī, al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Faraj al-Riyāshī and Muḥammad ibn Ḥabīb; Ibn al-Anbārī calls him trustworthy and devout, the transmitter of the Basrans. He was born in 212/827 and died in 275/888.

His lasting work is his editions of the old poetry with commentary: the poems of Imruʾ al-Qays, Zuhayr, al-Nābigha and al-Aʿshā, of Hudhayl and of the brigand poets, and of Abū Nuwās, whose rare words and meanings he explained in about a thousand leaves.
uncertain: Ibn al-Anbārī's print calls him ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan; the other sources name him al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥusayn.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 274–275
